transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before I can finalize the assignment, hospital policy requires me to hold a brief equipment-readiness check with physical therapy, facilities, nursing education, and infection prevention. I'd like to go around and hear from each of you on readiness, any concerns, and your recommendations for which unit should receive the lift. Let's start with physical therapy — can you walk us through the current transfer plans for both units?

The North unit patient can currently complete a two-person stand-pivot transfer with a gait belt. So from a clinical standpoint, the South unit patient has the greater need for the lift.

transcript.text: I need to share an important facilities constraint before we go further. The available lift is the Titan-MB model, which has a 48-inch turning radius. I've checked the room dimensions: South room 412 has a 50-inch doorway and can safely accommodate this lift, but North room 318 has only a 36-inch doorway and cannot safely accommodate it. Additionally, the charger must be placed in the South 4B equipment alcove. From a facilities standpoint, the lift can only physically go to the South unit.

transcript.text: From a nursing education standpoint, I can confirm that three South-unit nurses have completed the lift competency validation. Hospital policy requires two validated staff members for every lift transfer, and South unit has validated coverage available from 07:00 to 19:00 daily. This means South can meet the staffing requirement for safe lift operations during those hours.

transcript.text: From an infection prevention standpoint, I need to flag that the South unit patient is on contact precautions. Because of this, the lift plan requires a dedicated extra-large sling labeled specifically for South room 412, and a documented disinfecting wipe-down of the lift must be performed after each transfer. These are non-negotiable infection control requirements that need to be built into the operational plan before the lift is assigned.
